Hi Dylan,

We received invoice #2025-07-0102 and the total is ~38% higher than our estimate for July. Our team reviewed usage and billing and we can't reconcile the token counts with the calls in our logs. Specifically, calls from our embedding pipeline look like they were billed as generation tokens. Can you help explain the metering methodology that could cause this mismatch?

We've attached: our exported sample API calls for July (sample_api_calls_202507.csv) and the invoice PDF. Please let us know what additional logs you need from us.

Thanks,
Olivia Green

Hi Olivia — thanks for the note and for attaching the CSV, that's very helpful. I've looped in Naomi from Finance to help with a line-by-line reconciliation.

Short answer up front: Redwood's metering differentiates between embedding-only calls, generation (chat/completion) tokens, and special-cost features (e.g., tool calls). A few things we'll check immediately:
- whether any embedding requests were retried and counted twice
- if a variant model (higher-context) was used for some calls due to routing failover
- whether prefix/KV cache hits were missed for a small subset of requests during a short outage on 7/11 that we had in the US-west region.

Naomi — can you take the invoice and mark the top suspect line items? Olivia, we'll follow up with a short reconciliation table and proposed credit if we find over-billing.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on July invoice - token counts

Hi Olivia — Naomi from Finance here. I've pulled the invoice and the associated metering buckets. A few items I want to call out from our side after initial review:

1) On 2025-07-11 between 02:00-02:18 UTC our US-WEST routing experienced degraded KV cache routing for ~18 minutes. During that window some requests that normally hit the KV cache were routed to full-generation paths; that increases billed generation tokens even if the upstream call originated from an embedding flow. We are showing ~220k additional generation tokens in your account across that window.

2) There are 3 calls in your sample CSV that include a long system prompt (~5k chars) for debug runs. Those would be billed at generation-rate and explain a portion of the delta.

3) I do see two retries from the same client IP that resulted in duplicate ingest — we can zero those out pending your confirmation about whether you want us to deduplicate or leave as-is.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll create a reconciliation table mapping invoice line items to our meter buckets and the call timestamps.
- If the excess tokens map to the 7/11 incident and/or duplicates, we will credit the overage amount.
- For VAT: we applied standard US tax handling on the invoice; if Greenleaf qualifies for a VAT-exempt flow in the EU, we will need the exemption certificate. For US billing there's no VAT; if your admin sees VAT charged please forward the invoice line and I'll double-check.

Olivia — if you can confirm whether you want us to deduplicate the two retries, we can prepare the corrected invoice and proposed credit.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Billing Manager | Redwood Inference
Finance — Billing Operations

Thanks — that 7/11 window aligns with when one of our data pipelines had a retry storm after an upstream schema change. Please go ahead and deduplicate the two retries and map credits where appropriate.

Regarding the system prompt: those were debug runs from a sandbox; we can tag those calls going forward. For VAT: Greenleaf is US-based, no EU VAT here — apologies for the red herring.

One ask: can you also include a brief explanation of how Redwood distinguishes embedding vs generation metering in the invoice line detail? Our accounts team likes to see the meter bucket names next to line items for audit.

Olivia
